(Perth, Western Australia) | career_start = 2017 | career_end = | years1 = 2017–2019 | team1 = [[Rockingham Flames]] | years2 = 2019–present | team2 = [[Perth Wildcats]] | years3 = 2020 | team3 = [[Cockburn Cougars]] | highlights = * [[List of NBL champions|NBL champion]] ([[2019–20 NBL season|2020]]) * [[NBL Cup]] winner ([[2021 NBL Cup|2021]]) * [[State Basketball League Most Improved Player Award|SBL Most Improved Player]] ([[2019 MSBL season|2019]]) }} '''Luke Jacob Travers''' (born 3 September 2001) is an Australian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Perth Wildcats]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL). Opting to forgo college basketball in the United States to begin his professional career in Australia, he made his debut for the Wildcats as a development player in 2019 and became an [[List of NBL champions|NBL champion]] in 2020. At state league level, he played three seasons for the [[Rockingham Flames]] in the [[State Basketball League]] (SBL) between 2017 and 2019, and then had a stint with the [[Cockburn Cougars]] in 2020 during the [[2020 MSBL season|West Coast Classic]]. ==Early life and career== Travers was born in the [[Perth]] southern suburb of [[Rockingham, Western Australia|Rockingham]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.australiabasket.com/player/Luke-Travers/Australia/Perth-Wildcats/438100|title=Luke Travers|work=australiabasket.com|access-date=26 June 2021}} He attended [[Willetton Senior High School]]{{cite web|last=Newbold|first=Cameron|url=https://www.albanyadvertiser.com.au/news/albany-advertiser/nashs-schoolboys-best-in-the-west-ng-b881303126z|title=NASHS schoolboys best in the West|work=albanyadvertiser.com.au|date=27 August 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/u2vG0|archive-date=26 June 2021|quote=...to set up a grand final against Willetton Senior High School, featuring 197cm Perth Wildcats development player Luke Travers.}}{{cite web|url=https://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=204008408&client=0-8979-134640-512477-26372986|title=Player statistics for Luke Travers|work=Australian Schools Championships|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210626061807/https://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=204008408&client=0-8979-134640-512477-26372986|archive-date=26 June 2021}} and played for the [[Rockingham Flames]] as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.aussieprospects.com/feature-athlete-luke-travers|title=Feature Athlete: Luke Travers|work=aussieprospects.com|year=2018|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210626062105/https://www.aussieprospects.com/feature-athlete-luke-travers|archive-date=26 June 2021}} In [[2017 MSBL season|2017]], Travers debuted in the [[State Basketball League]] (SBL) for the Rockingham Flames. He saw action in five games and totaled five points.{{cite web|url=https://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=202883066&client=0-5011-83382-555108-26389663&ocompID=444191|title=Player statistics for Luke Travers – SBL June 2021}} In [[2018 MSBL season|2018]], he played five games during the regular season and then all five games during the finals, helping the Flames sweep the [[Geraldton Buccaneers]] 2–0 in the quarter-finals and averaging 14.7 points during the 2–1 semi-final series loss to the [[Perry Lakes Hawks]].{{cite June 2021}} In [[2019 MSBL season|2019]], he played 18 games for the Flames and averaged 11.7 points, 5.2 rebounds and 2.3 assists per game.{{cite Basketball League Most Improved Player Award|SBL Most Improved Player]].{{cite web|url=https://sbl.asn.au/2019/09/11/2019-sbl-awards/|title=2019 SBL AWARDS|work=SBL.asn.au|date=11 September 2019|access-date=11 September 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190911103414/https://sbl.asn.au/2019/09/11/2019-sbl-awards/|archive-date=11 September 2019}} In 2018, Travers helped break a 17-year drought for Western Australia, winning gold at the Under 18 National Championships.{{cite web|url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/article/young-gun-luke-travers-signed-as-development-player|title=Young gun Luke Travers signed as development player|work=Wildcats.com.au|date=1 August 2019|access-date=26 June 2021}} ==Professional career== On 1 August 2019, Travers signed with the [[Perth Wildcats]] as a development player for the [[2019–20 NBL season]]. His elite athleticism and ability to play multiple positions made him an attractive option for the Wildcats. Regarded as one of Australia's most sought-after basketball prospects, he had interest from a number of colleges in the United States, but indicated his desire to turn professional due to a lack of motivation at school.{{cite web|last=Smith|first=Ben|url=https://www.perthnow.com.au/community-news/cockburn-gazette/cougars-young-gun-hoping-to-traverse-the-path-to-professionalism-c-895131|title=Cougars young gun hoping to traverse the path to professionalism|work=perthnow.com.au|date=26 November 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/EjoUR|archive-date=26 June 2021}} In his debut for the Wildcats on 1 December 2019, he had three points, four assists and two rebounds in roughly 11 minutes in a 99–88 loss to the [[Adelaide 36ers]].{{cite web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://www.perthnow.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/perth-wildcats-stunned-in-home-blowout-with-loss-to-adelaide-ng-b881398608z|title=Perth Wildcats stunned in home blowout with loss to Adelaide|work=perthnow.com.au|date=1 December 2019|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/mjb7O|archive-date=26 June 2021}} On 20 December 2019, he opted to forgo college basketball and begin his professional career, signing a three-year contract extension with the Wildcats.{{cite web|url=https://www.wildcats.com.au/news/article/luke-travers-signs-long-term-deal-with-wildcats|title=Luke Travers signs long term contract with Wildcats|work=Wildcats.com.au|date=20 December December 2019|access-date=26 June 2021}} He played four games during the season{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Luke-Travers/Summary/133808|title=Luke Travers|work=RealGM.com|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210626070241/https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Luke-Travers/Summary/133808|archive-date=26 June 2021}} and was a member of the Wildcats' championship-winning squad in March 2020.{{cite web|url=http://www.wildcats.com.au/news/article/perth-wildcats-back-to-back-nbl-champions|title=Perth Wildcats Back-to-Back NBL Champions|work=Wildcats.com.au|date=19 March 2020|access-date=19 March 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/perth-wildcats-crowned-nbl20-champions|title=Perth Wildcats Crowned NBL20 Champions|work=NBL.com.au|date=19 March 2020|access-date=19 March 2020}} During the [[2020 MSBL season|West Coast Classic]] in 2020, Travers had a five-game stint with the [[Cockburn Cougars]], averaging 17.8 points, 14.4 rebounds, 5.2 assists, 2.2 steals and 1.2 blocks per game.{{cite web|url=https://websites.sportstg.com/team_info.cgi?action=PSTATS&pID=202883066&client=0-5011-83382-555108-26389663|title=Player statistics for Luke Travers – WCC June 2021}} Continuing on as a development player in the [[2020–21 NBL season]], Travers was thrust into a much larger role during the preseason, starting in both of the Wildcats' preseason games against the [[Illawarra Hawks]].{{cite web|last=Houben|first=Michael|url=https://pickandroll.com.au/p/nbl-2021-prospect-watch|title=NBL21 Prospect Watch: 17 names you should know this season|work=pickandroll.com.au|date=8 January 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210607065041/https://pickandroll.com.au/p/nbl-2021-prospect-watch|archive-date=7 June 2021}} While mostly a traditional wing player, he added strength to his frame over the off-season and was assigned the starting power forward role. He was replaced in the starting line-up by [[Jarred Bairstow]] midway through the season,{{cite web|last=O'Donoghue|first=Craig|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/basketball/bustling-perth-wildcat-jarred-bairstow-still-pinching-himself-amid-incredible-move-into-starting-five-ng-b881816462z|title=Bustling Perth Wildcat Jarred Bairstow still pinching himself amid incredible move into starting five|work=TheWest.com.au|date=10 March 2021|access-date=26 June 2021|url-access=subscription|quote=The Wildcats had been starting with teenage Development Player Luke Travers in the opening games. But after beginning the season strongly...}} with Travers later stating he got complacent in the role and was forced to work his way back into starting contention.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=geRS-YoRYyE|title=Luke Travers Press Conference - 13 June 2021|work=[[YouTube]]|publisher=[[Perth Wildcats]]|date=13 June 2021|access-date=26 June 2021}} On 28 March 2021, he went 6-of-6 from the field for 16 points off the bench in an 89–65 win over the [[Sydney Kings]].{{cite web|last=Encarnacion|first=Matt|url=https://thewest.com.au/sport/basketball/perth-wildcats-win-exposes-nbl-gap-kings-c-2458122|title=Perth Wildcats win exposes NBL gap: Kings|work=TheWest.com.au|date=28 March 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/aaAnq|archive-date=26 June 2021}} A season-ending injury to [[Bryce Cotton]] saw Travers return to the starting line-up as a guard at the back-end of the regular season and in the semi-finals.{{cite web|url=https://www.perthnow.com.au/sport/perth-wildcats/australia-basketball-great-shane-heal-says-melbourne-united-to-sweep-perth-wildcats-c-3139487|title=Australian basketball great Shane Heal says Melbourne United to 'sweep' Perth Wildcats|work=perthnow.com.au|date=17 June 2021|url-status=live|archive-url=https://archive.today/hAhkF|archive-date=26 June 2021|quote=Cotton's absence forced coach Trevor Gleeson to rely on his bench, most notably 19-year-old development player Luke Travers was thrust into a starting role over the three games and delivered 10.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and three assists per game.}} On 27 May, he had 16 points and eight rebounds in an 81–67 win over the Kings.{{cite web|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/bryce-less-wildcats-too-much-at-home-for-kings|title=Bryce-less Wildcats too much at home for Kings|website=NBL.com.au|date=27 May 2021|access-date=26 June 2021|quote=Development player Luke Travers was back to start and made the most of it setting a new career-high and he was the player kept the 'Cats on top during the third quarter finishing with 16 points and eight rebounds on 7/10 shooting.}} In the 2–1 semi-final series win over Illawarra, Travers averaged 10.7 points, 7.3 rebounds and three assists per game.
